page.overview:
Who is Aeolosaurus?

is an extinct genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived in South America during the Late Cretaceous period. Although it was small for a titanosaur, it was still quite large, and like some of the other smaller titanosaurs, it had bony plates on its back to protect it from the bite of large predators that would have attacked from above.

Known from several partial skeletons, Aeolosaurus is the first known titanosaur from fossil-rich Patagonia to exhibit dermal plates. An interesting note is that unusually thick egg shells with strange dome shapes on the surface were found associated with this dinosaur's fossil material.

Aeolosaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia. In its image, it is shown repelling two unknown dromaeosaur theropods.
